about.title: Plymouth Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Plymouth is a small Amador County community, and most residents don't expect a household appliance, farm tool, vehicle part, or piece of equipment to be the reason they end up hurt. But defective products cause serious injuries everywhere, including here along Rt 49, Miller Way, Shenandoah Road, and Empire Street where people work, drive, and shop every day. California's product liability law generally works in the injured person's favor: you typically don't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product had a design flaw, a manufacturing defect, or an inadequate warning, and that this defect caused your injury. Multiple parties along the supply chain — the maker, the distributor, even the retailer who sold it — may share responsibility. If a defective product hurt you or someone in your family in Plymouth, the first and most important step is holding onto the product itself, since it's often the strongest piece of evidence in the case. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney, free of charge, to review what happened.

items.question: I was hurt by a product but Plymouth doesn't have many recorded injury crashes — does that matter for my claim?
items.answer: No. Plymouth's traffic collision numbers, which recently showed zero recorded injury crashes, relate to roadway incidents and have no bearing on a product liability claim. A defective product injury is evaluated on its own facts, regardless of local crash statistics. What matters is the product's defect and how it caused your injury.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability law often allows claims under strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the manufacturer acted negligently. An independent attorney can review the specifics of what happened to you.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, if you safely can. The product itself is often key evidence, and attorneys strongly discourage repairing, discarding, or altering it before it can be examined.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to see if you have a case.
